text:
infra-bot: [ALERT] gpu-health-monitor: region=aus1 elevated ECC rate (x20 baseline) and rising XID counts. Available GPU capacity down 7.9%. Auto-drain triggered for several nodes.

maria-g: seeing a bump in 500s from hosted API and tail latency spikes. Is this the same thing?

alex-k: yup, maps to aus1 GPU pool. NVLink flaps and prober failures on racks rack-13, rack-17. Logs show lots of soft CE and XID 45/46 messages.

samir: any infra or kernel changes in last 24h? I don't see scheduled host/kernel updates. Could be firmware or a cohort of aged cards.

jess: we did lower the soft CE drain threshold yesterday to be more aggressive on drains (follow-up from last week's noise). Might be overreacting and causing node-level evacuations.

ops-oncall: quick triage plan: pause auto-drain, isolate the worst offenders, route critical traffic to fallback region, and schedule targeted reboots. Need confirmation on exact impact numbers first. :warning:

maria-g: can someone run the quick telemetry query so we know how many distinct GPUs are noisy vs how many nodes were evacuated?

alex-k: running query now:
```sql
SELECT gpu_id, host, ecc_count_hr, xid_count_hr, node_id FROM gpu_telemetry
WHERE region='aus1' AND ecc_count_hr > 0
ORDER BY ecc_count_hr DESC LIMIT 8;
```

partial output:
```
gpu-az-17 | host-az17-r1 | ecc=124 | xid=56 | node=az17-nd3
gpu-az-23 | host-az23-r2 | ecc=98  | xid=12 | node=az23-nd7
gpu-az-05 | host-az05-r3 | ecc=44  | xid=3  | node=az05-nd1
gpu-az-09 | host-az09-r2 | ecc=31  | xid=8  | node=az09-nd4
```

alex-k: TL;DR: ~46 GPUs showing elevated ECC/XID, but autoscaler/node-evac led to ~230 GPUs temporarily unavailable (whole-node drains).

samir: that explains the disproportionate capacity drop. We should avoid node-wide evacuations for transient ECC bursts. Change drain granularity to GPU-level for soft thresholds.

jess: agree. Ops runbook options: (1) set soft_ce_drain_threshold back to previous value, (2) switch to per-gpu drain for next 2 hours, (3) kick targeted reboots on affected hosts in staggered batches. I'll open a change and notifiy SRE.

ops-oncall: applying temporary mitigations now:
- soft_ce_drain_threshold -> 0.99 (pause most auto-drains)
- enable per-gpu isolation flag for patch windows
- enable fallback routing rule to send ~25% of traffic from aus1 -> usw2 (non-HA-critical requests first)

ops-oncall: expected immediate effect: available capacity drop should fall from 7.9% to ~3% after the first reboot wave. Cross-region egress cost expected to rise ~10-15% for next 24h.

maria-g: can you post the incident ID and runbook link when created? We'll need SLA impact calc for product.

infra-bot: Incident created INC-6734. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-flaky-cards . Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/GPuHealth/aus1-summary

alex-k: I'll gather NVLink/XID histograms for the affected cards and start RMA requests for any that still show XID >= 50 after reboots.

samir: monitoring dashboards and real-user traces now. Will post if error rate doesn't subside in 30m. :eyes:
